items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will actively listen using agreed-upon discussion rules with control of verbal and nonverbal cues.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will actively listen in order to analyze and evaluate speakers’ verbal and nonverbal messages by asking questions to clarify purpose and perspective.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will work effectively and respectfully in diverse groups by showing willingness to make necessary compromises to accomplish a goal, sharing responsibility for collaborative work, and recognizing individual contributions

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will follow agreed-upon rules as they engage in collaborative discussions about what they are reading and writing, expressing their own ideas clearly, building on the ideas of others, and respectfully disagreeing when necessary in pairs, diverse groups, and whole-class settings.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will conduct formal and informal presentations in a variety of contexts supporting their message with evidence and using verbal and nonverbal cues. processes. Writing Students will engage in a recursive process that may include prewriting, drafting, revising, editing, and publishing.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will summarize the main ideas and paraphrase significant parts of increasingly complex texts.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will identify characteristics of genres and analyze how they enhance comprehension of fiction, poetry, drama, and nonfiction.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will routinely and recursively prewrite (e.g., develop and organize ideas).

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will routinely and recursively develop drafts, applying organizational structure(s) (e.g., description, compare/contrast, sequential, problem/solution, cause/effect, etc.).

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will routinely and recursively revise drafts for organization, transitions, sentence variety, and consistent tone and point of view in order to improve coherence and meaning.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will routinely and recursively use resources to edit for grammar, usage, mechanics, and format in order to finalize drafts for publication.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will routinely and recursively publish final drafts for an authentic audience (e.g., publishing digitally, community and professional audiences, newspapers and magazines, entering contests).

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will analyze the extent to which historical, cultural, and/or global perspectives affect authors’ stylistic choices in grade-level literary and informational texts.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will evaluate authors’ perspectives and explain how those perspectives contribute to the meanings of texts.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will evaluate how literary elements impact theme, mood, and/or tone, using textual evidence: ● setting ● plot structure (e.g., foreshadowing, flashback, in media res) ● conflict (i.e., internal, external) ● characters (e.g., protagonist, antagonist) ● characterization (i.e., direct, indirect) ● point of view (e.g., narrator reliability) ● archetypes

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will evaluate how literary devices impact theme, mood, and/or tone, using textual evidence: ● figurative language (i.e., simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, imagery, symbolism) ● sound devices (i.e., onomatopoeia, alliteration, assonance) ● irony (i.e., verbal, situational, dramatic)

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will evaluate the validity of a speaker’s argument: ● distinguish the kinds of evidence (e.g., logical, empirical, anecdotal) ● distinguish substantiated from unsubstantiated claims ● analyze rhetorical appeals (i.e., ethos, logos, pathos) ● identify bias ● identify logical fallacies

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will analyze how informational text structures support the author’s purpose.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics, using textual evidence to support their claims and inferences.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will compose narratives reflecting real or imagined experiences that: ● include engaging plots involving well-developed, complex characters resolving conflicts ● establish narrator(s) that enhance(s) the narrative ● are intentionally sequenced in a way to achieve a specific effect (e.g., create suspense, establish mood, reflect theme) ● provide clear descriptions, using precise language, sensory details, and dialogue ● include varied syntax to enhance readability ● emulate literary elements and/or literary devices from mentor texts

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will compose informative essays, reports, or technical writing that: ● objectively introduce and develop topics ● include a defensible thesis ● incorporate evidence (e.g., specific facts, details, charts and graphs, data) ● maintain an organized structure ● use sentence variety and word choice to create clarity and concision ● establish and maintain a formal style ● emulate literary devices from mentor texts

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will compose argumentative essays, reviews, or op-eds that: ● introduce precise, informed claims ● include a defensible thesis ● acknowledge counterclaims or alternate perspectives ● organize claims, counterclaims, and evidence in a logical sequence ● provide the most relevant evidence to develop balanced arguments, using credible sources ● use sentence variety and word choice to create clarity and concision ● use style and tone that suits the audience and purpose

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will blend narrative, informative, and argumentative writing to suit their audience and purpose.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will analyze the relationships among synonyms, antonyms, and analogies.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use context clues, connotation, and denotation to determine or clarify the meaning of words or distinguish among multiple-meaning words.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use word parts (e.g., affixes, Anglo-Saxon, Greek, and Latin roots, stems) to define and determine the meaning of increasingly complex words.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use resources (e.g., dictionary, glossary, thesaurus, etc.) to determine or clarify the meanings, syllabication, pronunciation, synonyms, parts of speech, and etymology of words or phrases.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use precise, grade-level vocabulary in writing to clearly communicate complex ideas.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will select language to create a specific effect in writing according to purpose and audience.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will recognize and examine the effect of parallel structure and active and passive voice to convey specific meanings.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will recognize noun, verb, adjectival, and adverbial phrases and explain their effect in particular sentences.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use or revise for active/passive voice and parallel structure in words and phrases for effect.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will write using correct italics mechanics. Grade of Mastery: 8

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will write using correct semicolon mechanics. Grade of Mastery: 8 accurate information. Writing Students will synthesize information ethically through speaking and writing.

items.text: Students will add clarity, variety, and/or style to their writing and presentations with parts of speech and various types of phrases and clauses.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will recognize and correct misplaced and dangling modifiers.

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will write using correct capitalization mechanics. Grade of Mastery: 4

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will write using correct end mark mechanics. Grade of Mastery: 4

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will write using correct apostrophe mechanics. Grade of Mastery: 5

items.subject: ELA
items.text: Students will use commas to set off simple parenthetical elements.

items.subject: ELA

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: The student will describe the importance of earning an income and explain how to manage personal income through the use of a budget.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Describe the value of work and how individuals are responsible for their own financial decisions, as well as subsequent consequences.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Explain how costs and benefits determine the achievement of personal financial goals.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Analyze how income, career choice, and entrepreneurship impact an individual's financial plan and goals.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Evaluate the relationship between a person's human capital (e.g., education, skills, training, interests, initiative) and their earning potential.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Identify the purpose of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) in determining eligibility for grants, scholarships, and loans, as well as the essential information needed to apply.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Explain how to manage personal income and expenses to be a financially responsible citizen.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Identify factors that can affect income by describing the basic components of a paystub, including gross pay, net pay, and deductions (e.g., federal and state income tax, FICA, and voluntary deductions).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Differentiate between needs and wants in order to develop short, medium, and long-term goals that are specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and time-based.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Identify the components of a personal/family budget (e.g., income, savings/investments, taxes, emergency fund, expenses, and charitable giving) based on specific goals (e.g., financial, personal, educational, and career).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 1: Earning an Income and Budgeting
items.text: Explain how fiscally responsible individuals use various strategies and spending plans for tracking their income and expenses, both anticipated and unanticipated.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will identify and describe the impact of local, state, and federal taxes on income and standard of living.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the obligation of paying taxes and how individuals, as well as communities, might benefit from taxes.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify and explain various types of taxes, including income, payroll, sales, and property taxes, and when these types of taxes are due.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe some of the uses for taxation at the local, state, and federal levels (e.g., infrastructure, public safety, and courts of law).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the individual importance of meeting one's tax obligations.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the requirements to file taxes and compare basic tax forms, such as W2, W4, and 1040.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify possible consequences of failing to meet tax obligations (e.g., fees, penalties, interest, garnishment of wages, and imprisonment).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will describe the functions and uses of banks and other financial service providers.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare common financial service providers used by consumers to responsibly manage their assets (e.g., banks, mortgage companies, credit unions, brokerage firms, and finance companies).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare financial products and services offered to consumers, including their risks and protections.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify common financial products (e.g., checking, contactless payment systems, credit cards, savings, loans, investments, and insurance).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe available consumer banking technologies (e.g., Automated Teller Machines, mobile apps, digital wallets, and online banking).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the risks and protections associated with checks, debit cards, credit cards, online and mobile payment systems.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the role of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) to protect consumers' assets to a specified amount in commercial banks, savings banks, and credit unions.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the difference between banked and unbanked individuals, including the consequences of being "unbanked" (e.g., financial insecurity and access to credit).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will demonstrate the ability to manage a bank account and reconcile financial accounts.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the purpose of maintaining accurate financial accounts.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify the steps necessary for opening and maintaining a checking and savings account.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the reasons for balancing personal records and reconciling an account statement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Develop useful account management skills.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe how funds can be added and withdrawn from financial accounts (e.g., direct deposit, mobile deposit, teller deposit, debit withdrawals, and ATMs).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform basic account management skills, including correctly writing, endorsing, and depositing checks.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain how to manage financial accounts (e.g., reading and reconciling statements, navigating online platforms and apps).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the potential consequences of account mismanagement, such as non-sufficient funds, overdraft processing, and associated fees.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will analyze the costs and benefits of saving and investing.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain reasons for saving and investing (e.g., major purchases, education, and emergencies) as strategies used for meeting financial goals and building wealth over the short or long term.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare various strategies used to protect income and wealth.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the costs and benefits of various savings options, such as bank savings accounts, certificates of deposit, and money market mutual funds.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify the risk, return, and liquidity aspects of various investment options, such as stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and precious metals, including how diversification can help manage risk.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain how various financial investments align with financial goals, risk tolerance, and personal needs at different life stages, including how inflation affects investment growth.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare simple and compound interest.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain and give examples of the power of compound interest over time, including why saving and investing at an earlier age leads to far greater financial outcomes later in life, on average.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will explain and evaluate the importance of planning for retirement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the necessity of planning and saving for retirement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify costs of retirement such as living expenses, health care, and long-term care, based on life expectancy.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain how beginning to save or invest at different stages of life or over different periods of time significantly impact financial preparedness for retirement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Evaluate various sources of income for retirement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare government and employer-sponsored retirement plans, such as Social Security and 401(k) accounts.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify various personal investments, such as IRAs, and describe how they can provide financial resources for retirement.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain that entrepreneurs and self-employed individuals may be responsible for generating their own retirement income, as opposed to government or employer-sponsored plans.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will identify the process and analyze the responsibilities of borrowing money.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare sources and products related to borrowing money.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify sources of credit (e.g., banks, credit unions, retail businesses, private lenders, and the federal government).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe various credit products (e.g., credit cards, car loans, and mortgages).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare sources of student loans (U.S. Department of Education versus private banks and credit unions) regarding eligibility, interest rates, and terms of repayment.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze how one's credit history impacts borrowing money and maintaining credit.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the importance of establishing a positive credit history (e.g., favorable interest rates, employment, and financial opportunities).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe how credit reports compiled by credit bureaus are used to determine creditworthiness.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify the information contained in a credit report and how to access a free credit report.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain that a credit score is a numeric rating assessing an individual's credit risk based on information from their credit report.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify factors that affect a credit score, such as payment history, credit utilization, amount owed, length of credit history, debt owed, and types of credit used.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the process of borrowing money.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify factors involved in borrowing (e.g., credit history, credit report, debt to income ratio, loan to value ratio, and length of employment).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain how the terms of borrowing (e.g., interest rates, APR, fees, repayment schedules, terms, and conditions) affect the cost of borrowing.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare types of credit, including revolving and installment credit, and collateralized loans versus unsecured loans.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Differentiate between standard loan practices and predatory lending practices, such as rapid tax return and payday loans.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the responsibilities and consequences of borrowing money.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify consumer responsibilities, rights, and remedies, including fair debt collection practices protected by law.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain why responsible borrowers monitor their credit reports and how errors can be corrected.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the impact of non-repayment of debt on individuals, families, businesses, and the broader economic system.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 8: Interest, Credit Cards, and Online Commerce
items.text: The student will describe and explain interest, credit cards, and online commerce.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 8: Interest, Credit Cards, and Online Commerce
items.text: Evaluate the costs and benefits of using credit cards for purchasing goods and services.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 8: Interest, Credit Cards, and Online Commerce
items.text: Explain how interest rates and fees impact the cost of using credit cards.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 8: Interest, Credit Cards, and Online Commerce
items.text: Describe options for payment on credit cards, such as minimum payment, delayed payment, and payment in full.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 8: Interest, Credit Cards, and Online Commerce
items.text: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of online commerce, including how to conduct transactions safely.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: The student will identify and explain consumer fraud and identity theft.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Analyze how consumers can become victims of deceptive practices that significantly impact their financial well-being.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Identify various types of consumer fraud, such as medical fraud, imposter schemes, forgery, pyramid schemes, and false billing.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Describe common methods used by criminals to commit fraud (e.g., bait and switch, skimming, changing address, and phishing).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Differentiate between consumer fraud and identity theft, including common methods used to steal one's identity, such as dumpster diving, hacking, and social media.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Describe ways to protect yourself from identity theft and fraudulent practices (e.g., monitor monthly financial statements and annual credit reports; protect personal information and passwords).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 9: Consumer Fraud and Identity Theft
items.text: Explain necessary responses if victimized by fraudulent business practices or identity theft (e.g., alert appropriate law enforcement agencies and credit bureaus, freeze credit histories, and change passwords).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: The student will explain and compare the costs and benefits of renting versus buying a home.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of renting versus buying a home by comparing how various housing options meet different needs and wants.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: Describe the elements and terms of a standard lease agreement (e.g., deposit, due date, grace period, late fees, and utilities).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: Analyze financial considerations when purchasing a place to live.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: Identify types of lenders and mortgage loans, including fixed versus adjustable-rate mortgage loans.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.standard_label: Standard 10: Renting versus Buying a Home
items.text: Explain the elements of a mortgage (e.g., down payment, escrow account, home insurance, property taxes, late fees, potential early payment penalties, and amortization tables).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will describe and explain how various types of insurance can be used to manage risk.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe common risks to individuals, their property and investments, caused by situations such as illness, accidents, and natural catastrophes.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain the importance of insurance as a risk management strategy used by financially responsible individuals.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe common types of insurance purchased by consumers, such as health, property, life, disability, automobile, and renter's insurance.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify different methods for obtaining health insurance, including employer-provided plans, government plans, and private purchase.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Evaluate appropriate amounts of insurance to meet one's needs and budget including how insurance deductibles work.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will explain and evaluate the financial impact and consequences of gambling.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Identify common types of gambling available to consumers and explain the probabilities of winning at games of chance.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Evaluate the impact of gambling on the economic development of local, tribal, and state communities, including revenue, employment, and tourism.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the costs of gambling on individuals and society (e.g., financial situation, addictive behavior, and missed work).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will evaluate the consequences of bankruptcy.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the costs and benefits of bankruptcy as a last resort for individuals and families facing financial challenges.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain ways to avoid bankruptcy and identify alternatives to bankruptcy (e.g., budget management, debt management, refinancing, and financial counseling).

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the importance of reestablishing a positive credit history and recommended steps for improving a credit score after bankruptcy.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: The student will explain the costs and benefits of charitable giving.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Explain civic responsibilities and opportunities related to charitable giving.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe reasons why individuals engage in charitable giving, such as personal reward, community improvement, and tax deduction.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Compare different ways in which individuals can donate to charity, including monetary gifts, gifts-in-kind, and volunteer service.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe how charitable giving can fit into one's spending plan.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the importance of charitable giving.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe the impact of charitable giving on the entity receiving the gift, such as improved quality of life and emergency relief.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Analyze the impact of charitable giving on the community at large, including local development and improved standard of living.

items.subject: Personal Financial Literacy
items.text: Describe how to evaluate the authenticity of charitable organizations by identifying recipients, allocation of resources, and activities, based on information from watchdog organizations and regulatory agencies.

Level 2: Passes and receives to and from a moving target with or without an implement using various movements with competency in small-sided games.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Executes at least two offensive techniques (e.g., pivots, fakes, jab steps, give & go, or screens) to create open space during varying practice tasks or in a dynamic environment. Level 2: Applies at least two offensive skill techniques with defensive pressure during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Dribbles with hand, foot, or implement using a change of speed and direction during varying practice tasks or in a dynamic environment. Level 2: Dribbles with hand, foot, or implement using a change of speed and direction during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Shoots on a goal with power and accuracy during varying practice tasks or in a dynamic environment. Level 2: Shoots on a goal with power and accuracy during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates defensive ready position with weight on balls of feet, arms extended, and eyes on midsection of the offensive player, while moving in all directions without crossing feet. Level 2: Maintains a defensive ready position while drop stepping (appropriate to the sport) in the direction of the pass during player-to-player practice or in small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Performs a legal underhand or overhand serve with a mature pattern to a pre-determined target for net/wall/racket games (e.g., badminton, volleyball, or pickleball). Level 2: Consistently executes a legal underhand or overhand serve with a mature pattern for distance and accuracy for net/wall/racket games (e.g., badminton, volleyball, or pickleball).

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Strikes using a mature pattern in a non-dynamic environment for net/wall/racket games (e.g., volleyball, handball, badminton, tennis, pickleball) or fielding/striking games (e.g., baseball, softball, cricket, hockey). Level 2: Strikes using a mature pattern in a dynamic environment or during small-sided net/wall/racket games or fielding/striking games.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates the mature pattern of the forehand/backhand strokes and volley using a short or long implement during varying practice tasks or in a dynamic environment in net games (e.g., paddleball, pickleball, badminton, or tennis). Level 2: Demonstrates the mature pattern of the forehand/backhand strokes and volley using a short or long implement with power and accuracy in small-sided net games.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Using an implement, accurately strike a stationary object (e.g., croquet, shuffleboard, or golf). Level 2: Using an implement, strike a stationary object for accuracy, power, and distance.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates correct technique for basic skills in at least one self-selected indoor/outdoor pursuit (e.g., archery, juggling, disc golf, fencing, fishing, hiking, jump rope, kayaking, martial arts, rock climbing). Level 2: Demonstrates correct technique for basic skills in at least two self-selected indoor/outdoor pursuits.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes how to open and close space by combining locomotor movements with movement concepts during various practice tasks or in a dynamic environment. Level 2: Applies tactics for creating space during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Executes at least one of the following offensive tactics to create open space: moves to create open space on and off the ball; uses a variety of passes, cuts, fakes, and pathways, give and go. Level 2: Executes at least three of the following offensive tactics to create open space: moves to create open space on and off the ball; uses a variety of passes, cuts, fakes, and pathways, give and go.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes defensive tactics (e.g., denial of pass/catch, anticipating the speed of the object or person) to reduce space or passing angles during various practice tasks or dynamic environments. Level 2: Applies appropriate defensive tactics to increase turnovers or decrease scoring opportunities during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Recognizes tactics/strategies that make transitions from defense to offense or vice versa more effective (e.g., recovering quickly, communicating with teammates, capitalizing on an advantage). Level 2: Implements effective transition tactics/strategies into game play situations.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes how to create open space during various net/wall/racket practice tasks with either a long or short implement by varying force and direction, or by moving the opponent from side to side and/or forward and back. Level 2: Applies open space strategies during net/wall/racket games with either a long or short implement.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Reduces offensive options for opponents by returning to midcourt position and selects an offensive shot based on opponent’s location (hit where opponent is not) during various practice tasks or in a dynamic environment. Level 2: Varies placement, force, and timing of return to prevent anticipation by opponent during small-sided game play.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Differentiates between a variety of shots (e.g., slap and run, bunting, line drive, high arc) to hit into open space. Level 2: Recognizes various situations (e.g., sacrifice) and when to appropriately implement them into a game situation.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies the correct defensive play based on the situation (e.g., number of outs, offensive skill set, score, time in the game/inning). Level 2: Applies the correct defensive play based on the situation.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Recognizes how speed, force, and trajectory of the shot are impacted based on location of the object in relation to the target. Level 2: Selects appropriate shot and/or club based on location of the object in relation to the target in a practice task or dynamic environment.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies potential factors (e.g., weather, hazardous conditions) influencing appropriate safety decisions. Level 2: Implements safe protocols in self-selected outdoor pursuits.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes a variety of movement principles (e.g., tempo, levels, pathways, flow) to dance and rhythmic activities. Level 2: Applies a variety of movement principles to dance and rhythmic activities.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies barriers and determines solutions related to maintaining a physically and mentally healthy lifestyle. Level 2: Applies solutions for reducing identified barriers.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Engages in physical activity one to two times per week outside of physical education class. Activities can include moderate to vigorous exercise such as walking, jogging, biking, skating, dancing, or swimming; strength and endurance training like bodyweight exercises or resistance training; or participation in lifetime team, individual, or dual sports. Level 2: Participates in physical activity three or more times a week outside of physical education class.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Differentiates between moderate to vigorous physical activities in addition to identifying recommended time spent in each of these areas daily. Level 2: Creates a plan for implementing moderate to vigorous physical activity for at least 60 minutes per day five times a week.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Using available technology, sets and monitors a self-selected physical activity goal for aerobic activity and/or muscle and bone strengthening based on current fitness level. Level 2: Using available technology, adjusts physical activity based on the type of exercise needed for a minimum health standard and/or optimal functioning based on current fitness level.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Differentiates between static and dynamic stretching while recognizing correct techniques and methods of stretching. Level 2: Appropriately applies a variety of static and dynamic stretching techniques for all major muscle group.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Design a health and fitness plan that utilizes each of the health-related fitness components (e.g., cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, muscular strength, flexibility, and body composition). Level 2: Critique and correct a health and fitness plan that utilizes each of the health-related fitness components.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes each component of the FITT principle (frequency, intensity, time and type) for different types of physical activity (aerobic, muscular fitness, and flexibility). Level 2: Uses the FITT principle in preparing a personal workout.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes the role of warm-ups and cool downs before and after physical activity. Level 2: Designs and implements a warm-up and cool down regimen for a self-selected physical activity.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Defines resting heart rate and describes its relationship to aerobic fitness and the Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) Scale. Level 2: Applies the RPE Scale to adjust workout intensity during physical activity.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies major muscles used in selected physical activities. Level 2: Explains how opposing muscles interact with one another (e.g., agonist and antagonist) during physical activity.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Designs and implements a program of remediation for one area of improvement based on the results of health-related fitness assessment. Level 2: Designs and implements a program of remediation for two or more areas of improvement based on the results of health- related fitness assessment.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Maintains a physical activity log for at least two weeks and reflects on activity levels as documented in the log. Level 2: Maintains a physical activity log for at least one month and reflects on activity levels as documented in the log.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Creates strategies to maintain a balanced diet, including nutritious meals, smart snack choices, and regular water intake. Level 2: Demonstrates the ability to consistently make balanced choices by planning and maintaining a routine that includes nutritious meals, healthy snacks, and adequate water intake.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies effective stress management strategies such as deep breathing, guided visualization, yoga, and aerobic exercise. Level 2: Demonstrates basic techniques from stress-reducing activities such as mindfulness, yoga, tai chi, or deep breathing.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates responsibility by showing respect, practicing safety, cooperating, and including others. Level 2: Reflects on personal responsibilities and takes action to improve physical activity, fitness, mental health, and social well-being.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies and uses appropriate strategies to self-reinforce positive fitness behaviors, such as positive self-talk. Level 2: Applies self-reinforcement strategies (e.g., positive self-talk, visualization) in challenging physical activities.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates self-responsibility by implementing specific corrective feedback to improve performance using teacher- generated guidelines. Level 2: Provides encouragement and corrective feedback to peers without prompting from the teacher.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies cooperation skills by establishing rules and guidelines for resolving conflicts. Level 2: Demonstrates appropriate response to participants’ ethical and unethical behavior during physical activity by using rules and guidelines for resolving conflicts.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies expectations and etiquette in a variety of physical activities. Level 2: Applies expectations and etiquette in a variety of physical activities.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Uses physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately and safely, with the teacher’s guidance. Level 2: Independently uses physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately and identifies specific safety concerns associated with the activity.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates competency and/or refines activity-specific movement skills in one or more lifetime activities (indoor/outdoor pursuits, individual-performance or dual activities, aquatics, net/wall/racket games, or target games). Level 2: Refines activity-specific movement skills in two or more lifetime activities (indoor/outdoor pursuits, individual- performance or dual activities, aquatics, net/wall/racket games, or target games).

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates competency in cultural, social, and/or technical dance forms and rhythmic movements (e.g., weddings, parties, ballroom, modern, hip hop, tap). Level 2: Demonstrates competency by designing and performing a dance and/or a rhythmic routine.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates application, evaluation, and competency in one or more specialized skills in health-related fitness activities. Level 2: Demonstrates application, evaluation, and competency in two or more specialized skills in health-related fitness activities.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies the historical and cultural roles of games, sports, and dance in society. Level 2: Discusses the relevance of historical and cultural roles of games, sports, and dance in society.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Uses movement concepts and principles (e.g., force, motion, rotation) to analyze and improve performance of self and/or others in at least one selected skill. Level 2: Uses movement concepts and principles to implement strategies to improve performance for self and/or others in two or more selected skills.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Creates and implements a practice plan to improve performance for a self-selected skill. Level 2: Evaluates and revises a practice plan to improve performance for a selected skill.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies examples of social (e.g., salsa, swing, ballroom - foxtrot, waltz, hip-hop, line dancing, etc.) and technical (e.g., ballet, tap, contemporary, jazz, etc.) dance forms. Level 2: Compares similarities and differences in various dance forms.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies and discusses the benefits of regular physical activity and common barriers that may impact participation related to college, career, and community involvement. Level 2: Explains how regular physical activity supports personal goals for college, career, and community life, and analyzes strategies to overcome barriers to participation.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Evaluates the accuracy of fitness- and health-related claims made in social media content and advertisements. Level 2: Analyzes and applies technology and social media to find, evaluate, and support healthy lifestyles.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies safety concerns and health risks related to physical activity in varying weather conditions (e.g., cold, hot, humid, windy). Level 2: Applies pacing strategies and perceived exertion levels to adjust physical activity in varying environmental conditions.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Identifies and evaluates physical activities available in the local community based on benefits, social support, and participation requirements. Level 2: Analyzes and selects physical activities in the local environment that support personal fitness goals, social connections, and accessibility.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Regularly participates in a self-selected lifetime activity, dance, or fitness activity outside of the school day. Level 2: Develops and follows a personal training plan to prepare for and participate in a community-based physical activity event (e.g., 5K, tournament, dance performance, cycling event).

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates proper form and technique when using resistance-training machines and free weights. Level 2: Designs and follows a strength and conditioning program that promotes muscular balance and supports a healthy, active lifestyle.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Explains how fitness level and nutrition affect physical performance and uses target heart rate and technology to plan and monitor aerobic exercise intensity. Level 2: Identifies energy systems used in physical activity and uses technology to monitor and adjust exercise intensity within the target heart rate zone.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Describes the structure of skeletal muscle, different muscle fiber types, and the difference between concentric and eccentric muscle contractions. Level 2: Identifies and explains types of strength training (isometric, isotonic, isokinetic) and stretching methods (static, dynamic, proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation [PNF]) used to improve strength, endurance, and flexibility.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Creates and implements a fitness plan that supports a healthy, active lifestyle for someone in college or a chosen career field. Level 2: Analyzes health- and skill-related fitness components and develops a fitness portfolio aligned with personal, college, or career goals.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Creates and follows a nutrition plan that supports energy balance and a healthy, active lifestyle to enhance physical performance. Level 2: Develops a snack plan for before, during, and after physical activity that meets nutritional needs for each phase of exercise.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Explains the purpose and benefits of various stress- management strategies (e.g., mental imagery, relaxation techniques, deep breathing, aerobic exercise, meditation) for managing stress. Level 2: Demonstrates and integrates stress-management strategies into a personal routine to manage stress during academic, social, and physical challenges.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Demonstrates effective self-management skills to analyze barriers and modify physical activities appropriately as needed. Level 2: Analyzes how media can influence body image and describe one self-management skill to make healthy choices based on their own needs instead of media messages.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Uses effective communication and critical thinking skills to solve problems and support positive group dynamics during physical activity, both individually and as part of a team. Level 2: Demonstrates a leadership role (e.g., task or group leader, referee, coach) by applying communication and critical thinking skills to adapt strategies, resolve conflicts, and enhance team performance in a variety of physical activities.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Exhibits proper etiquette, respect for others and teamwork while engaging in a variety of physical activities. Level 2: Demonstrates leadership in promoting proper etiquette, respect, and including others during physical activities, while effectively supporting team dynamics and resolving conflicts.

items.subject: Physical Education
items.text: Level 1: Evaluates best practices for participating safely in a variety of physical activities (e.g., injury prevention, water safety, proper alignment, hydration, use of equipment, implementation of rules, and sun protection). Level 2: Applies best practices for participating safely in a variety of physical activities.
